subject: Priv hosting architecture readiness & next step
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@averytech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Priv hosting architecture readiness & next step

Hi Sam — thanks again for the discovery call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next step: 

Recap (short)
- Primary workload: real-time customer support embeddings + model inference for session-level routing.
- Compliance: PCI out-of-scope, PII retention requirements; need VPC/private deployment and audit logging.
- Target milestone: pilot environment in Q4, production early Q1.

Next step: technical architecture deep-dive (90 min) to cover network requirements, IAM/KMS, data flow, and ops/runbook. Can we lock a slot for a technical workshop so our infra and ops teams can align with yours? Proposed windows:
- Tue, Oct 3 — 10:00–11:30 PT
- Wed, Oct 4 — 14:00–15:30 PT
If neither works, happy to offer week of Oct 9.

I attached a short pre-call checklist (network ports, service accounts, sample runbook) to speed the session. Would you also share who from your infra/network team should be on the call (and their contact) so we can include runbook-level asks up front?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. Wed, Oct 4 14:00–15:30 PT works for us. Attendees we plan to join:
- Sam Patel (CTO)
- Priya Kumar (Infra lead) <priya.kumar@averytech.com>
- Todd Adams (Network) <todd.adams@averytech.com>

A couple quick asks from our side before the deep-dive:
- Can you share a short agenda so we can prep engineers?
- Any specific egress/port info or third-party endpoints we should pre-approve?
- We’d like to see a short example runbook (onboarding -> failover -> rollback) if you have a template.

Otherwise green to lock Oct 4. See you then.

— Sam

Great — thanks Sam, Oct 4 14:00–15:30 PT is confirmed. I just created a calendar invite and included the preliminary agenda and prep items: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcd1234efgh5678

Preliminary agenda (90 min)
- 0–10m: intros & scope calibration (Jordan/Sam)
- 10–40m: infra topology & network prerequisites (Connor + Todd)
- 40–70m: security controls (KMS, audit logs, retention) (Marissa + Priya)
- 70–85m: runbook review + failover scenarios (Connor)
- 85–90m: next steps & action items

Attachments included: redwood-priv-deploy-precall-checklist.pdf, priv-hosting-runbook-sample.pdf, network-prereqs.txt (these are short stubs—network-prereqs.txt lists firewall rules/ports we typically request).

Notes: Connor — can you cover the topology slides and be ready to call out our recommended subnet/NAT patterns? Marissa — will you lead the security controls segment and have the KMS integration notes handy? Sam — adding Priya and Todd to the invite; if Todd can share one contact point in advance we’ll send a short port matrix so they can route approvals.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Jordan Blake | Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Team — quick internal note ahead of Oct 4 deep-dive with AveryTech (confirmed). Action items: 
- Marissa: lead the security controls section; bring the KMS integration checklist and a short slide on audit-log retention options (we may need SOC2 artifact references).
- Connor: prepare topology + runbook snippets; highlight how our KV cache and batching behave in a private VPC and any network flows that require egress to telemetry endpoints.
- I’ll send the port matrix to Todd once he confirms contact and will own the meeting facilitation.

Goal for the session: leave with a mutual action plan (MAP) and a follow-up POC checklist we can attach to the deal in HubSpot. Please add any prep docs to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cD4EfGhIjKlMnOp

Thanks — Jordan
